name: @acc/decho-styling
description: The Decho design tokens: seven themes as values and as CSS custom properties, with helpers for re-tinting a theme and defining your own. No React and no components — those are @acc/decho-components, which depends on neither this package nor a stylesheet. Ships its own adoption codemod, Blueprint adapter and lint rule.
//files: src is shipped deliberately, for the same reason as the other packages here (source maps point at ../src/*) and for one more: the CSS entry points ARE src files. tsc copies no assets, so exporting them from src is the alternative to adding a bundler to a package whose whole job is not to need one.
//publishConfig: A DIFFERENT Artifacts repository from the other five packages here, which publish to ri.artifacts.main.repository.df396b79-*. Deliberate: this one is meant to be installed by widget repositories across the estate rather than only by map consumers. The consequence to remember is that a consumer wanting this package AND a decho map package needs both registries configured.
//peerDependencies: React is optional and wide. The root entry point is tokens and style objects with no runtime dependency at all — a non-React widget, a test or a node script can take it — and only the /react subpath needs React. Pinning it would be the ERESOLVE trap @acc/decho-basemap's note describes, for a package that imports one type and one hook.
//exports: The .css and .json entries point into src/ rather than dist/: tsc copies no assets, and adding a bundler to a package whose whole point is not needing one would be a poor trade. src is shipped anyway, as the other packages here do.
//devDependencies: react-dom is here for the component tests, which render with renderToStaticMarkup rather than pulling in Testing Library. It is deliberately NOT a peer dependency: the package itself renders no DOM, and a consumer using only the tokens should not be asked for it.
